item: CGT 50% discount replaced from 1 July 2027 (Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 1) Act 2026, Act No. 49 of 2026, and Income Tax Rates Amendment (Tax Reform No. 1) Act 2026, Act No. 50 of 2026)
officialValue: Both are law. The Federal Register shows Act No. 49 of 2026 and Act No. 50 of 2026 as "In force", with registration, effect and assent all on 26 June 2026. The 50% discount stays for an individual's gain from a CGT event before 1 July 2027 (new s 115-100(aa)). From 1 July 2027, gains that build up from that date get cost base indexation, and resident individuals pay a 30% minimum tax on them. The first return that can be affected is 2027-28. The ATO published a new page, "Capital gains tax reform" (QC108170), on 13 October 2026. It says the first stage "is now law" and gives the same 1 July 2027 start date. The ATO "CGT discount" page (QC66019) is unchanged since its 29 June 2026 update and still has the "announced in the 2026–27 Federal Budget" banner.

item: VIC teachers: Victorian Government Schools Agreement 2026 (VGSA 2026), FWC matter AG2026/2746. Has the FWC approval decision been published?
officialValue: Yes, it is approved. The FWC decision [2026] FWCA 2836 (State of Victoria (Department of Education) T/A Department of Education, AG2026/2746) was made by Deputy President Millhouse in Melbourne on 16 October 2026. It approves the Victorian Government Schools Agreement 2026 with undertakings, says the agreement operates from 23 October 2026 under s 54, and keeps the nominal expiry of 10 August 2030. The agreement ID is AE534356 and the order is PR815386. Earlier checks missed it because it is numbered 2836, below the 2839 to 2934 range that was scanned. The Department of Education's Enterprise Bargaining overview ("Updated 26 October 2026") confirms it: "On the 16 October 2026 the Fair Work Commission approved the Victorian Government Schools Agreement 2026, replacing the Victorian Government Schools Agreement 2022. Its Salary Rates page ("Updated 26 October 2026") reads "This policy is under review and will be updated in line with any relevant changes in the Victorian Government Schools Agreement 2026", and the Teachers schedule is still "last updated 17 August 2022". The Resources page ("Updated 25 August 2026") still lists only the "Proposed VGSA 2026" documents.

item: NSW Health graduate radiographer (medical radiation scientist) Level 2, year 1 start rule under Determination 25 of 2023 (lapses 30 Oct 2026 unless replaced): has a replacement determination or award change been published? Compared with lib/data/public-health-allied-pay/nsw.ts
officialValue: As at 27 Oct 2026, Determination 25 of 2023 (signed 17 Nov 2023, Phil Minns, Deputy Secretary, NSW Ministry of Health) still applies. It sets "the commencement rate for the employment of new MRS graduates to 'Level 2 Year 1'" for graduates who are fully registered with AHPRA and hold a radiation licence (para 5c covers diagnostic radiographers). Para 9 says it "remains in force until 30 October 2026 unless rescinded or replaced earlier". I found no replacement, extension or rescission. The NSW Health "Awards and determinations" page (Health Services Union, Determinations) still links only "Medical Radiation Scientists - Commencement Rate Determination", the same 2023 PDF, and the page says "Current as at: Thursday 23 October 2025". The Health Employees' Medical Radiation Scientists (State) Award 2025 (in force from 1 July 2025 for two years) has not taken in the rule. Clause 8(i) of that award, and its Level 1 definitions, still say a graduate starts at Level 1 in the Provisional Development Year (PDY) or Supervised Practice Program (SPP) and moves automatically to Level 2 once that is complete. Searches of health.nsw.gov.au and the IRC NSW gazette found no 2026 determination and no award variation on graduate commencement.

item: Woolworths Australian Food Group Agreement 2024 (AE525523): shiftwork loadings (cl 11.3) and the Annual Wage Review citations [2025] FWCFB 3500 / [2026] FWCFB 3500 in lib/data/employer-pay/woolworths.ts
officialValue: Agreement AE525523 cl 11.3 (operative from 21 October 2024), table "Rates of pay for shiftwork". Full-time and part-time: "between midnight Sunday and midnight Friday", which is Monday to Friday, base + 30%; Saturday base + 50%; Sunday base + 75%; public holiday (voluntary): public holiday rates. Casuals (casual loading included): + 55%, + 75%, + 100%. Cl 11.1 limits the clause to team members specifically employed as shiftworkers. Cl 11.2 defines shiftwork as a shift starting at or after 6pm and before 5am the next day. Baking production shiftworkers have their own rates in cl 11.4: early morning shifts M-F + 12.5% (casual + 37.5%), Sat + 50% / + 75%, Sun + 100% / + 125%; night shifts before 2am M-F + 30% / + 55%, Sat + 50% / + 75%, Sun + 100% / + 125%. Citations: the FWC lists "Annual Wage Review Decision 2025 [2025] FWCFB 3500", announced 3 June 2025, and "Annual Wage Review Decision 2026 [2026] FWCFB 3500", announced 2 June 2026. The FWC gives every year's AWR decision the number 3500, so both citations are correct.

verdict.reason: I could not refute the claim. I fetched the FWC PDF of AE525523 live (Firecrawl, maxAge 0). Cl 11.3, "Rates of pay for shiftwork", reads: "Shiftwork between midnight Sunday and midnight Friday | Base rate + 30% | Base rate + 55%"; Saturday + 50% / + 75%; Sunday + 75% / + 100%; public holiday (voluntary): public holiday rates apply. Cl 11.1(a) limits the clause to team members "specifically employed as shiftworkers". Cl 11.2(a) defines shiftwork as a shift starting at or after 6:00pm on one day and before 5:00am on the following day. Cl 11.4 sets baking production rates: early morning (shifts starting at or after 2am and before 6am) M-F + 12.5% / + 37.5%, Sat + 50% / + 75%, Sun + 100% / + 125%; night shifts (starting before 2am) M-F + 30% / + 55%, Sat + 50% / + 75%, Sun + 100% / + 125%. These match the claim exactly. The approval decision in the same PDF (para [40]) confirms the agreement operates from 21 October 2024, with nominal expiry 17 April 2028. The site line at lib/data/employer-pay/woolworths.ts:88 reads "+ 30% Sunday to Friday". That label is wrong because it overlaps the Sunday + 75% row. The rates on the site are all correct. "Sunday to Friday" appears nowhere else in lib/, modules/ or app/, and no test in lib/data/employer-pay/__tests__ mentions shiftwork, so the claim that no test needs updating holds. Citations: the live FWC AWR 2024-25 page says the 2025 decision was announced on Tuesday 3 June 2025 and lists "Annual Wage Review Decision 2025 [2025] FWCFB 3500". Its last-updated date is 01 May 2026; the claim recorded no date for this page. The AWR 2026 page says the decision was announced on Tuesday 2 June 2026, lists "Annual Wage Review Decision 2026 [2026] FWCFB 3500" and was last updated 02 Jun 2026. Both citations on the site are correct. The proposed new text matches cl 11.1 to 11.4 and is accurate. The 3.5% and 4.75% percentages are outside this claim and were not re-checked, because the AWR landing pages do not print them.
verdict.correctedValue: No correction needed. The AE525523 cl 11.3 permanent loadings are +30% Monday to Friday ("between midnight Sunday and midnight Friday"), +50% Saturday and +75% Sunday; casual loadings are +55%, +75% and +100%. These apply only to staff specifically employed as shiftworkers, with shifts starting at or after 6pm and before 5am (cl 11.1–11.2). Baking production shiftworkers have separate rates under cl 11.4. Both citations, [2025] FWCFB 3500 and [2026] FWCFB 3500, are correct.
